name: Archelosauria
blurb: Turtles grouped with archosaurs, the lineage of crocodiles and birds. Where turtles belong was argued over for more than a century.

relationship.note: Genome-scale data place turtles with archosaurs. Anatomy has placed them elsewhere, because their skulls lack the openings other reptiles have.

competing.name: Turtles with archosaurs
competing.summary: Turtles are the sister group of crocodiles and birds, as most genome-scale studies find.

competing.name: Turtles with lepidosaurs
competing.summary: Turtles are closest to the tuatara, lizards and snakes, as some morphological analyses found.

competing.name: Turtles outside the diapsids
competing.summary: Turtles branched off before all other living reptiles, the traditional reading of their solid skull.
